podcast.body: Released in March 1964 at the peak of "Beatlemania" in America, this highly anticipated song was an advanced single from their forthcoming movie, "A Hard Day's Night." It debuted on the Hot 100 at number 27, which was a rare top 40 debut for the 1960s, and then spectacularly leapt a record 26 spaces from number 27 to number one on the chart dated April 4, 1964. It is suggested that with more accurate, computerized data (unavailable in the analog era), it likely would have debuted at number one instantly. "In late March of that year, can't buy me love debuted on the Hot 100 at number 27."

podcast.body: Two weeks after "She Loves You" replaced "I Want to Hold Your Hand" at number one in March 1964, The Beatles ejected their own "She Loves You" from the top spot with this song, cementing their imperial highpoint during the first wave of Beatle Mania. "Two weeks later, the Beatles ejected themselves again with Can't Buy Me Love."
